title: Incipit: Ex Ilss. quodam Philosophi R.C. extractum
shelf_note: An alchemical miscellany: a medieval 'Speculum luminum' recipe for lye made from the ashes of human blood (p45), a 17th-century English/Latin treatise on the materia prima citing the Turba and Morienus (p88), and Ripley's 'Pupilla Alchymiae' (p132). It belongs on an alchemy/Rosicrucian shelf. No tradition or collection is given in the packet, so the fit is judged on content alone.
structure_note: No structure counts in the packet. The volume is composite or bound from several hands: p45 is a late-medieval Gothic cursive with its own foliation ('17' at image 45), while p88 and p132 are in a 17th-century English secretary/italic hand. So the '17th Century' date fits only part of the volume. That is a cataloguing nuance, not a defect. No translations exist for any of the three pages.

book_verdict: The transcriptions are faithful on all three pages, including a heavily abbreviated medieval Gothic cursive (p45) and two 17th-century English/Latin pages that are near-perfect. The slips are minor normalisations and one doubled interlinear word. Nothing here would mislead a reader, but there is no English translation yet.
